standard.title: OWASP WSTG 4.2 — Fast active HTTP review
standard.description: Focused first pass: 16 of 94 WSTG 4.2 scenarios covering authentication and authorization bypass, account takeover, IDOR, injection, SSRF, XSS/CSRF, malicious uploads and sensitive backup files. The other 78 scenarios are outside this preset's coverage. This Contractor selection is not an official OWASP priority ranking or a full WSTG assessment. Selected objectives and evidence rules are unchanged. Missing prerequisites and unsupported capabilities remain gaps. Active HTTP checks require approval; browser execution, raw-network tests, callbacks and isolated multi-user sessions are not supplied.

license.attribution: OWASP Foundation and WSTG contributors, Web Security Testing Guide 4.2, CC BY-SA 4.0. Scenario titles and objectives are reproduced from the pinned release checklist. Contractor adds version-qualified identifiers, versioned links and review mappings/evidence policies under the same license. Merged aliases and the removed buffer-overflow stub are omitted. Contractor selects 16 scenarios for a bounded first pass; omitted scenarios are outside coverage, not assessed. Package edition: 4.2-fast-http.1.

entries.title: Testing for Default Credentials
entries.statement:
Enumerate the applications for default credentials and validate if they still exist.
Review and assess new user accounts and if they are created with any defaults or identifiable patterns.

entries.title: Testing for Bypassing Authentication Schema
entries.statement: Ensure that authentication is applied across all services that require it.

entries.title: Testing for Weak Password Change or Reset Functionalities
entries.statement:
Determine the resistance of the application to subversion of the account change process allowing someone to change the password of an account.
Determine the resistance of the passwords reset functionality against guessing or bypassing.

entries.title: Testing Directory Traversal File Include
entries.statement:
Identify injection points that pertain to path traversal.
Assess bypassing techniques and identify the extent of path traversal.

entries.title: Testing for Bypassing Authorization Schema
entries.statement: Assess if horizontal or vertical access is possible.

entries.title: Testing for Privilege Escalation
entries.statement:
Identify injection points related to privilege manipulation.
Fuzz or otherwise attempt to bypass security measures.

entries.title: Testing for Insecure Direct Object References
entries.statement:
Identify points where object references may occur.
Assess the access control measures and if they're vulnerable to IDOR.

entries.title: Test Upload of Malicious Files
entries.statement:
Identify the file upload functionality.
Review the project documentation to identify what file types are considered acceptable, and what types would be considered dangerous or malicious.
If documentation is not available then consider what would be appropriate based on the purpose of the application.
Determine how the uploaded files are processed.
Obtain or create a set of malicious files for testing.
Try to upload the malicious files to the application and determine whether it is accepted and processed.

entries.title: Review Old Backup and Unreferenced Files for Sensitive Information
entries.statement: Find and analyse unreferenced files that might contain sensitive information.

entries.title: Testing for Reflected Cross Site Scripting
entries.statement:
Identify variables that are reflected in responses.
Assess the input they accept and the encoding that gets applied on return (if any).

entries.title: Testing for Stored Cross Site Scripting
entries.statement:
Identify stored input that is reflected on the client-side.
Assess the input they accept and the encoding that gets applied on return (if any).

entries.title: Testing for SQL Injection
entries.statement:
Identify SQL injection points.
Assess the severity of the injection and the level of access that can be achieved through it.

entries.title: Testing for Command Injection
entries.statement: Identify and assess the command injection points.

entries.title: Testing for Server-side Template Injection
entries.statement:
Detect template injection vulnerability points.
Identify the templating engine.
Build the exploit.

entries.title: Testing for Server-Side Request Forgery
entries.statement:
Identify SSRF injection points.
Test if the injection points are exploitable.
Asses the severity of the vulnerability.

entries.title: Testing for Cross Site Request Forgery
entries.statement: Determine whether it is possible to initiate requests on a user's behalf that are not initiated by the user.

mappings.title: Testing for Default Credentials
mappings.objective:
Perform bounded authorized HTTP checks for WSTG-v42-ATHN-02. WSTG test objectives:
Enumerate the applications for default credentials and validate if they still exist.
Review and assess new user accounts and if they are created with any defaults or identifiable patterns.

Use only the declared target and authorization scope, after the Server's active-check approval. Preserve request/response evidence and control comparisons. Report satisfied only when all applicable objectives are established by live evidence in the declared scope. Unavailable browser, raw-network/TLS, external-discovery or isolated identity capabilities leave explicit gaps. A response code or absence of a demonstrated exploit alone is not a pass. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/v42/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/04-Authentication_Testing/02-Testing_for_Default_Credentials.html
